name: cloud-fit
question: A company's cloud bill keeps growing and finance cannot explain it. Nobody can tell whether the driver is instance sizing, provisioned-but-unused capacity, storage growth, egress, retry storms, or the way the bill is attributed across teams. Find the highest-leverage lever and prove why it is the highest-leverage one, rather than the one that happens to look biggest this month.

facts.referential: an over-budget resource-month: a machine, disk or managed service whose bill for the period exceeded the committed amount for it, measured per resource
facts.proposition: A provisioned-but-unused capacity state can be identified before the period closes, and reclaiming it reduces the bill.
facts.scope: one cloud account, three teams, three regions, 600+400 resource-months over two consecutive periods; historical billing records, not live telemetry
facts.authority: the finance owner owns the definition of over budget; the billing export owns the numbers; the platform team owns the instance-class catalogue
facts.obligation: must prove the lever generalises to a period the fit never saw, and must never claim the bill explains the bill
facts.temporal: definitions valid for the whole window; no pricing change recorded during it
facts.consumption: the platform lead; decision = reclaim idle capacity or resize instance classes; if the result is wrong, the reclaim work is spent and the bill does not fall

note: Synthetic. The real driver is provisioned-but-unused capacity (idle_hours). billed_usd is what the overspend flag is computed from, so it is not a candidate explanation -- it is the overspend. vcpus outranks the driver on the fitting period only because instance class was recorded from the review list that period, while the idleness metric that period was estimated by a sampling agent that was wrong in both directions; untagged_fraction is the same artifact in the cost-attribution data. egress_gb is missing for 17% of resource-months. Nobody tells the engine any of this.
